newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras coffee crop hit by storms, damage unknown.
newsitem.headline: Honduras coffee crop hit by storms, damage unknown.

text.p: Honduras' coffee crop has been damaged in widespread 10-day storms although it difficult to evaluate damage as of yet, the president of the Association of Honduran Coffee Exporters said Thursday.
"We have had too much rain and there will be damage, but it is very difficult to estimate to what extent so soon after the storms," Osmond Maduro told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Hurricane Marcos and another storm have dumped heavy rains across Central America in recent days, but especially focused their ire on Honduras.

Maduro said the low-lying coffee growing zones of Copan, Ocotepeque and Cortes were especially hit, with the Honduran 1996-1997 harvest (November-March) just starting. Honduras was expected to harvest a 3.0 million 46-kg bag harvest this year in line with the output recorded last cycle.
Maduro said it was "very likely" that rains caused beans to fall from trees. He added that infrastructure damage, largely to plantation access roads, had already been reported.

Around 500,000 46-kg quintals of Honduran coffee are traditionally exported as contraband beans through Guatemala each year, a trend likely to discontinue this year because Honduras abolished an export tax in May that was the main cause of the illicit trade.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
